facts.text: Talmadge was named after three silent‑film sisters—Norma, Constance, and Natalie Talmadge—who were famous actresses in the early 20th century.
The neighborhood’s roots trace back to the 1920s, when developers built homes that still line its tree‑shaded streets today.
Every summer, Talmadge hosts a Block Party that celebrates a century of community spirit and neighborhood pride.
Talmadge’s streets were originally designed to feel like a movie‑star retreat, a vision that still echoes in its classic architecture.
The Talmadge Fire Safe Council runs a Dumpathon each year, gathering residents to clean up and protect the neighborhood’s green spaces.
Newcomers to Talmadge are welcomed by a volunteer committee that hands out a packet of goodies and local tips for settling in.
